CHIEF COMPLAINT
Nonhealing foot ulcer on right foot.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Gregory presents with a two-month history of a foot ulcer on his right foot. He reports that the ulcer recently became red and started draining, which is his primary concern. He believes the injury originated from walking barefoot on Dewey Beach. He describes discomfort as occasional throbbing but denies severe distinct pain. He has diabetes which he manages with medication but does not regularly check his blood sugar. He reports his last A1C was approximately 10. His primary care provider recently prescribed antibiotics, but the patient has not yet picked them up from the pharmacy and does not recall the specific medication name.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports occasional throbbing at the ulcer site. He notes new onset of drainage and redness.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Diabetes.

MEDICATIONS
Diabetes medication (type not specified). Antibiotics prescribed by PCP but not yet filled.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works as ambulance driver. Sustained injury from walking barefoot at Dewey Beach.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs normal. Afebrile. Right foot examination: 1 x 2 inch circular wound on the dorsal aspect of the lateral right foot, just proximal to the fifth metatarsophalangeal joint. Erythema and drainage present. Surrounding edema noted. No necrosis, odor, or bony exposure. Palpation elicits increased pressure sensation without distinct pain.

RESULTS
X-ray of right foot: no evidence of osteomyelitis.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Diabetic foot ulcer with infection. Plan includes: (1) Order ankle-brachial index (ABI) to assess blood supply to the foot; (2) Perform debridement; (3) Prescribe Clindamycin 400 mg orally twice daily for 7 days to treat infection; (4) Provide surgical shoe for next month to reduce pressure on foot; (5) Follow-up in two weeks with possible additional debridement. Patient instructed to call office with any concerns between visits. Advise to seek urgent care or emergency department if develops fever, feels unwell, or notices blackening of tissue.
